title: ICAN Foundation
issuer: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public ICAN foundation-level syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A sole trader has total assets of N850,000 and total liabilities of N350,000 at the year end, and the owner made no drawings or capital injections during the year. What is the amount of the owner's equity?
items.explanation: Under the accounting equation, equity equals assets minus liabilities, so N850,000 less N350,000 gives N500,000. Adding the two figures, or reporting liabilities or assets alone, misstates equity.

items.stem: A trader buys goods on credit from a supplier for N120,000. Which double entry correctly records this transaction in the trader's books?
items.explanation: Goods bought on credit increase purchases (an expense) and create a payable, so purchases is debited and payables credited. No cash moves, so the cash account is not part of the entry.

items.stem: A machine is purchased for N600,000 and is expected to have a residual value of N60,000 after a useful life of five years. Using the straight-line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
items.explanation: Straight-line depreciation spreads the depreciable amount, N600,000 less N60,000 = N540,000, over five years, giving N108,000 each year. Dividing the full cost by five ignores the residual value and overstates the charge.

items.stem: An asset costing N500,000 is depreciated at 20 percent per annum on the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation charge for the second year of the asset's life?
items.explanation: The first year charge is 20 percent of N500,000, which is N100,000, leaving a carrying amount of N400,000. The second year charge is 20 percent of N400,000, which is N80,000.

items.stem: A business paid N180,000 in rent during the year and owed a further N30,000 of rent at the year end which had not yet been paid. What amount should be charged as rent expense for the year?
items.explanation: On the accrual basis, the expense for the period includes rent incurred but unpaid at the year end, so N180,000 plus the N30,000 accrual gives N210,000. Charging only the cash paid ignores the accrual.

items.stem: A business paid N240,000 on 1 October for a twelve-month insurance policy starting that date. Its financial year ends on 31 December. What is the insurance expense for the current year?
items.explanation: Only three months of cover (October to December) belong to the current year, giving three-twelfths of N240,000, which is N60,000. The remaining N180,000 is a prepayment carried into the next year.

items.stem: Closing inventory cost N500,000 but, because of damage, it can only be sold for N460,000 after all further costs are met. At what amount should the inventory be valued?
items.explanation: IAS 2 requires inventory to be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Since the net realisable value of N460,000 is below cost, the inventory is written down to N460,000.

items.stem: A business has opening inventory of N200,000, purchases of N800,000 and closing inventory of N250,000. What is the cost of goods sold for the period?
items.explanation: Cost of goods sold equals opening inventory plus purchases minus closing inventory, so N200,000 + N800,000 - N250,000 = N750,000. Adding closing inventory instead of deducting it gives the wrong figure.

items.stem: A trader reports sales of N1,200,000 and a cost of goods sold of N750,000 for the year. What is the gross profit for the year?
items.explanation: Gross profit is sales revenue less the cost of goods sold, so N1,200,000 - N750,000 = N450,000. Adding the two figures instead of subtracting them is a common error.

items.stem: A bank statement shows a credit balance of N500,000. Cheques totalling N80,000 have been issued but not yet presented, and deposits of N50,000 are not yet credited. What is the corrected cash book balance?
items.explanation: Starting from the bank statement balance, add deposits not yet credited and deduct unpresented cheques: N500,000 + N50,000 - N80,000 = N470,000. Reversing these adjustments produces the wrong balance.

items.stem: A business has trade receivables of N400,000 and decides to create a provision for doubtful debts of 5 percent. What is the amount of the provision?
items.explanation: The provision is 5 percent of the N400,000 receivable book, which equals N20,000. Deducting rather than applying the percentage, or using a wrong rate, misstates the allowance.

items.stem: Which of the following errors would cause the two sides of a trial balance to disagree in total?
options: Posting a transaction to the wrong account of the same class
Omitting a transaction completely from the books
Recording a motor vehicle purchase in the motor expenses account
Posting only the debit side of a transaction to the ledger
items.explanation: A trial balance fails to agree only when the debits and credits of an entry are unequal. Posting one side alone breaks that equality, whereas wrong accounts, omission and misclassification keep both sides equal.

items.stem: Which of the following payments made by a manufacturing business is capital expenditure?
options: Installation costs of a newly acquired machine
Repairs to an existing machine damaged in use
The annual maintenance contract for the factory
Fuel used by the delivery van during the year
items.explanation: Capital expenditure is incurred to acquire or bring an asset into working condition, so machine installation is capitalised. Repairs, maintenance and fuel are revenue costs charged to profit or loss.

items.stem: During the year a trader pays N120,000 for insurance, N60,000 for wages and N40,000 for a new delivery van. Which total should be charged to the income statement as revenue expenditure?
items.explanation: Insurance and wages are revenue expenditure and are charged to profit or loss, giving N120,000 + N60,000 = N180,000. The van is a non-current asset and is excluded from the charge.

items.stem: Which of the following would be classified as a current asset in a statement of financial position?
options: Motor vehicles used in the business
Freehold premises owned by the business
items.explanation: Inventory is expected to be converted into cash within the normal operating cycle, so it is a current asset. Motor vehicles and premises are non-current assets, and a bank loan is a liability.

items.stem: A business records rent as an expense in the period in which it is incurred even though payment is made later. Which accounting concept does this apply?
options: The going concern assumption about the life of the business
The prudence convention of anticipating losses only
The consistency convention of applying methods uniformly
The accrual basis, matching income and expenses to the period
items.explanation: Recording expenses when incurred rather than when paid is the accrual basis, which matches costs to the period they relate to. Going concern, prudence and consistency address different issues.

items.stem: Two partners share profits in the ratio of three to two. If the partnership earns a profit of N500,000 for the year, what amount belongs to the partner entitled to the larger share?
items.explanation: The ratio of three to two has five parts in total, so the partner with the larger share receives three-fifths of N500,000, which is N300,000. Dividing the profit equally or using the wrong share misstates the entitlement.

items.stem: An asset with a cost of N200,000 and accumulated depreciation of N150,000 is sold for N60,000. What is the profit or loss on disposal?
items.explanation: The carrying amount is N200,000 less N150,000, which is N50,000, and the sale proceeds are N60,000, giving a profit of N10,000. Comparing proceeds with original cost ignores accumulated depreciation.

items.stem: A supplier quotes a list price of N50,000 and allows a trade discount of 10 percent. What amount should be recorded in the purchaser's books for the goods at the time of purchase?
items.explanation: Trade discount is deducted before the transaction is recorded, so the goods are entered at N50,000 less 10 percent, which is N45,000. A cash discount would only arise on prompt settlement and is not recorded here.

items.stem: Under the IASB conceptual framework, which of the following is an enhancing qualitative characteristic of useful financial information?
items.explanation: Comparability is one of the enhancing characteristics that increase the usefulness of information already relevant and faithfully represented. Relevance and faithful representation are the fundamental characteristics, while materiality is an aspect of relevance.

items.stem: A sum of N50,000 is invested at simple interest of 8 percent per annum. What is the total interest earned over three years?
items.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time, so N50,000 x 0.08 x 3 = N12,000. Using the annual figure only, or compounding it, gives the wrong total.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: N100,000 is invested at 10 percent per annum compounded annually. What is the total compound interest earned after two years?
items.explanation: The investment grows to N100,000 x 1.10 x 1.10 = N121,000, so the interest is N21,000. Simple interest of N20,000 ignores the interest earned on the first year's interest.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A payment of N121,000 is due in two years' time and the discount rate is 10 percent per annum. What is the present value of that payment?
items.explanation: Present value equals the future amount divided by 1.10 squared, so N121,000 / 1.21 = N100,000. Discounting for only one year or not at all gives the other figures.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A data set consists of the values 4, 8, 10, 14 and 14. What is the arithmetic mean of the data set?
items.explanation: The mean is the sum of the values divided by their count, so (4 + 8 + 10 + 14 + 14) / 5 = 50 / 5 = 10. Using the mode or an incorrect total gives the other answers.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: The values 3, 7, 9, 15, 21 and 25 are arranged in order. What is the median of these values?
items.explanation: With an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values, so (9 + 15) / 2 = 12. Choosing one middle value or the mean of the whole set is incorrect.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: For the data set 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 7, 7 and 9, what is the mode?
items.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently, and 7 appears three times, more than any other value. The values 3 and 9 appear less often.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A data set contains the values 12, 5, 19, 8 and 14. What is the range of this data set?
items.explanation: The range is the largest value minus the smallest, so 19 - 5 = 14. Reporting the maximum alone or an incorrect pair of values misstates the spread.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A fair six-sided die numbered 1 to 6 is rolled once. What is the probability that the outcome is an even number?
items.explanation: There are three even outcomes (2, 4 and 6) out of six equally likely outcomes, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2. Using only one even number or all six outcomes gives the wrong fraction.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: Two fair coins are tossed once. What is the probability that both coins show heads?
items.explanation: The two tosses are independent, so the probability is 1/2 multiplied by 1/2, which equals 1/4. There are four equally likely outcomes and only one is two heads.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A sum of N180,000 is to be shared among three partners in the ratio of 2, 3 and 4. What is the largest share?
items.explanation: The ratio has nine parts in total, so one part is N180,000 / 9 = N20,000 and the largest share of four parts is N80,000. Dividing equally ignores the ratio.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A trader buys a shirt for N4,000 and sells it at a mark-up of 25 percent on cost. What is the selling price?
items.explanation: A mark-up of 25 percent on cost adds N1,000 to N4,000, giving a selling price of N5,000. Confusing mark-up on cost with a margin on selling price gives the wrong figure.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A business has fixed costs of N200,000, a selling price of N50 per unit and variable costs of N30 per unit. How many units must it sell to break even?
items.explanation: Contribution per unit is N50 - N30 = N20, and break-even units equal fixed costs divided by contribution, so N200,000 / N20 = 10,000 units. Dividing by the selling price is a common error.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A student scores 70 marks in a course weighted 3 and 50 marks in a course weighted 1. What is the weighted average score?
items.explanation: The weighted average is (70 x 3 + 50 x 1) / (3 + 1) = 260 / 4 = 65. Taking a simple average of 70 and 50 gives 60, which ignores the weights.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A distribution has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. What is the coefficient of variation?
items.explanation: The coefficient of variation is the standard deviation divided by the mean, so 5 / 50 = 0.10, or 10 percent. It expresses relative variability and is not the standard deviation itself.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: The price index of a commodity rose from a base-level value of 100 in 2020 to 120 in 2024. What is the percentage increase in price over the period?
items.explanation: The increase is 120 minus 100, which is 20 index points on a base of 100, so the percentage rise is 20 percent. Reading the index itself as the percentage change is incorrect.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business Mathematics and Statistics

items.stem: A student with limited income must choose between buying a textbook and buying a concert ticket. In economic terms, what is the opportunity cost of buying the textbook?
options: The price paid for the textbook
The total income of the student
The combined cost of both items
The value of the concert ticket forgone
items.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up, which here is the concert ticket. The money price of the textbook is the accounting cost, not the opportunity cost.

items.stem: Which statement correctly describes the law of demand?
options: Quantity demanded falls as price rises, other things held constant
Quantity demanded rises as price rises, other things held constant
Quantity supplied falls as price rises, other things held constant
Quantity demanded is unrelated to price in all markets
items.explanation: The law of demand states an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, with all else equal. The second statement reverses the relationship, and supply behaviour is a different concept.

items.stem: If the cost of producing a good falls, what is the most likely effect on its supply curve?
options: The supply curve shifts to the left, reducing supply
The supply curve shifts to the right, increasing supply
The supply curve does not move at all
items.explanation: Lower production costs make supplying the good more profitable at every price, shifting supply to the right. A leftward shift would follow a rise in costs, not a fall.

items.stem: In a market the demand function is Qd = 100 - 2P and the supply function is Qs = 20 + 2P. What is the equilibrium price?
items.explanation: Setting Qd equal to Qs gives 100 - 2P = 20 + 2P, so 80 = 4P and P = 20. Substituting the other candidate values does not balance the two functions.

items.stem: When the price of a good rises by 20 percent, quantity demanded falls by 20 percent. What is the price elasticity of demand?
items.explanation: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price, so 20 / 20 = 1, which is unit elastic. Any other ratio misreads the figures.

items.stem: A good has a negative income elasticity of demand. What type of good is it?
items.explanation: Negative income elasticity means demand falls as income rises, which defines an inferior good. Normal and luxury goods have positive income elasticity, while complementarity is measured by cross elasticity.

items.stem: The cross elasticity of demand between two goods is positive. What is the relationship between the goods?
items.explanation: A positive cross elasticity means a rise in the price of one good increases demand for the other, so they are substitutes. Complements have negative cross elasticity, and unrelated goods have zero.

items.stem: Which statement best explains the law of diminishing marginal utility?
options: As more units are produced, total cost always falls
As price rises, total revenue always rises
As more units of a good are consumed, the extra satisfaction from each additional unit falls
As income rises, consumption of every good falls
items.explanation: Diminishing marginal utility describes how the additional satisfaction gained from each extra unit of a good declines as consumption increases. The other statements confuse utility with cost or revenue behaviour.

items.stem: When marginal cost is below average cost, what is happening to average cost as output rises?
options: Average cost is at its minimum
items.explanation: As long as the marginal cost of the next unit is below the average, that unit pulls the average down, so average cost is falling. Average cost rises once marginal cost exceeds it.

items.stem: Which of the following is a fixed cost for a factory in the short run?
options: The rent paid on the factory building
The cost of raw materials used in production
Wages paid to workers on the production line
The electricity used to run the machines
items.explanation: Rent does not vary with output in the short run, so it is a fixed cost. Raw materials, production wages and machine electricity all vary with output and are therefore variable costs.

items.stem: In a perfectly competitive market, what is the position of an individual firm with respect to price?
options: It sets a price above the market price
It is a price taker and accepts the market price
It faces a downward-sloping demand curve
It alone decides the market price
items.explanation: With many buyers and sellers and a homogeneous product, a single firm cannot influence price and is a price taker. A downward-sloping demand curve belongs to imperfectly competitive firms.

items.stem: Which feature best distinguishes a monopoly from other market structures?
options: Many small firms selling identical products
A few large firms selling differentiated products
A single seller protected by barriers to entry
Perfect information available to all buyers
items.explanation: A monopoly exists where one firm supplies the whole market and barriers prevent new entrants. Many homogeneous sellers describes perfect competition, and a few differentiated sellers describes oligopoly.

items.stem: Which statement best defines inflation?
options: A one-off increase in the price of a single good
A fall in the general level of prices
A rise in the quantity of money in circulation only
A sustained rise in the general level of prices
items.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level across the economy, not a single product's price. A general fall in prices is deflation, and money growth alone is only one possible cause.

items.stem: Which statement correctly describes gross domestic product?
options: The market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a period
The total income earned by a country's citizens anywhere in the world
The value of a country's exports less its imports
The total money supply held by households and firms
items.explanation: GDP measures the market value of final output produced within a country's borders over a period. Income earned abroad by citizens is captured by GNP, while exports less imports is net exports.

items.stem: Which of the following is an instrument of monetary policy?
options: Changes in the rate of company income tax
Open market operations by the central bank
items.explanation: Monetary policy works through money supply and interest rates, and open market operations are a central bank instrument. Taxation, government spending and tariffs are tools of fiscal or trade policy.

items.stem: Which management function is primarily concerned with setting objectives and deciding in advance how to achieve them?
items.explanation: Planning is the function of setting objectives and choosing the means to reach them before action is taken. Controlling compares results with plans, while staffing and co-ordinating deal with people and effort.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: What is the likely organisational consequence of a narrow span of control?
options: A flat structure with few levels of management
An increase in the number of subordinates per manager
A tall structure with many levels of management
items.explanation: A narrow span means each manager supervises few staff, which requires more management layers and produces a tall structure. A wide span produces a flatter structure with fewer levels.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which level represents the highest form of motivation?
items.explanation: Self-actualisation sits at the top of Maslow's hierarchy, representing the drive to realise one's full potential. Safety, social and physiological needs are lower levels that must generally be met first.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: Which leadership style involves the leader consulting subordinates and sharing decision-making with them?
items.explanation: A democratic leader invites participation and shares decisions with the team. Autocratic leaders decide alone, laissez-faire leaders leave the team to itself, and bureaucratic leaders rely rigidly on rules.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: Which feature distinguishes a sole trader from a limited liability company?
options: The sole trader must publish audited accounts
The sole trader has perpetual succession
The sole trader has unlimited personal liability for business debts
The sole trader raises capital by issuing shares
items.explanation: A sole trader is not a separate legal person and is personally liable for all business debts. Publishing audited accounts, perpetual succession and issuing shares are features of a company.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: What is an advantage of a limited liability company over a sole proprietorship when raising finance?
options: It pays no tax on its profits
Its owners are free of all legal duties
It cannot be sued in its own name
It can issue shares to raise capital from many investors
items.explanation: A company can issue shares and thereby draw on capital from a wide group of investors, which a sole proprietor cannot do. Companies remain taxable, owe legal duties and can sue and be sued in their own name.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: Which of the following is not one of the traditional four elements of the marketing mix?
items.explanation: The traditional marketing mix is product, price, place and promotion. People belongs to the extended services mix rather than the original four Ps.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: In a SWOT analysis, which element represents an external factor facing a business?
items.explanation: Threats are external conditions that could harm the business, as are opportunities. Strengths, weaknesses and core competences are internal attributes of the firm.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: In corporate governance, to whom is the board of directors primarily accountable for the stewardship of a company?
items.explanation: The board is elected by and answerable to the shareholders, who own the company, for the stewardship of its assets and performance. Suppliers, unions and competitors are stakeholders but not the owners.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management

items.stem: Which statement best describes a stakeholder of a business organisation?
options: Only the shareholders who own the business
Only the customers who buy its products
Only the managers who run its operations
Any group or individual affected by the organisation's activities
items.explanation: A stakeholder is any party affected by, or able to affect, the organisation, including employees, customers, suppliers and communities. Shareholders, customers and managers are each only one subset of stakeholders.
items.reference: ICAN Foundation Syllabus - Business and Management
